title: Quandoequareous (Newtown Creek)
summary: A Queens creek-name for the west branch of Newtown Creek, connected in older records with the Mespat kills.
introduction_content: Quandoequareous is recorded as the west branch of Newtown Creek in Queens County. Variants include Quandoe-quareous and Quandus Quaricus.
history_content: The name appears in a seventeenth-century boundary description for the Newtown Creek and Mespat kills landscape. The dated deed reference is handled as a timeline entry with its source citation.
translation_content:
No separate translation is given for Quandoequareous. The name preserves variant spellings attached to a branch of Newtown Creek.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names can tell us the history of particular areas: the way that people used to live and work; the ecology of a place; culture of songs, stories, poetry.”

— Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park Authority, Literary Landscapes education resource (n.d.), introductory description
preservation_content: Quandoequareous keeps a Queens waterway name visible within the wider Long Island placename record, connecting Newtown Creek, Mespat, and colonial boundary descriptions.
